conclusion: The new caption is supported by visible judgments while the user plays. The old wording can imply exact audible playback of the just-completed performance; that capability was not found in the inspected source. The app does have auditory feedback, so this is a removal of replay/accuracy ambiguity, not a finding that the app produces no audible feedback.

findings.finding: Audio tap copies short samples for in-memory pitch/onset analysis. The lesson handler receives hertz/level and the analyzer emits onset/chord/stroke/strum results. Stop clears the listener and frame callback.
Live hertz becomes heard MIDI/cents; PlayAlongSession judges notes and updates grades, offsets, hit times and score. Ribbon/runway/pitch lanes consume that state while phase is playing.

findings.topic: Stored take data is not performance audio
findings.finding: SongTake retains score/grades/judgments; a judgment contains index, grade and timing offset, not recorded audio or played pitches. The transient pitch trail is capped at a few seconds and its located app consumer is HighwayCanvas, not a synthesis/replay path.
Hit/miss earcons, band thinning/filling, swishes, celebration, and spoken VoiceOver summary exist. These are live feedback/result cues, not playback of exactly how the user performed.

RecordingPlayer plays deliberately imported audio; LessonExplain replay plays a lesson demonstration; results lesson action opens another lesson; Perform again starts a new performance. None establish a user-take recording/reconstruction playback feature.
Policy distinguishes no recorded/stored/uploaded live microphone audio from deliberately imported recordings. New headline makes no collection, recording, upload or perfect-accuracy promise.

search_scope.result: No recording API or user-performance resynthesis path found in inspected production Swift; recordingURL matches route to the imported-file library. Negative search is supplementary to traced flow, not proof of all runtime behavior.
